findings.obligation: A document changed in a diff agrees with the rest of that diff, and the wrong side is fixed in the same change (nw-code-craftsmanship 39); a claim is recorded at the strength its own checker gives, and an unavailable tool is recorded as unavailable rather than a run recorded as blocked (nw-typesafe-system-one, nw-type-level-design honest-claim rules).
findings.observation: The ADR's Consequences paragraph reads "The claim is not checked: quint, java and apalache-mc are absent from the shared Lima VM local-dev, the only environment this project runs tools in, so the design records this axis Blocked and the runtime DESIGNED_NOT_BUILT until that toolchain is there or a human waives the proof." The same delta contradicts it twice. docs/feature/iis-secrets-key-replace/design/live_replica_gate.receipt.txt, added at 35a5335, records quint 0.32.0 and openjdk 21.0.12.1 present in local-dev, `quint typecheck live_replica_gate.qnt` exit 0, `quint run --invariant=gateAlwaysLive` and `--invariant=windowInsideRetention` exit 0, `quint verify --invariant=gateAlwaysLive,windowInsideRetention --max-steps=44` exit 0 "The outcome is: NoError", the negated tightness witness refuted at exit 1, and both refused windows killed as mutants m8 and m9 at exit 1 each. docs/feature/iis-secrets-key-replace/architecture.md:2068 states the checked claim correctly. The ADR was written at 6efcdcb, one commit before the receipt, and its Consequences text was never brought into line.
findings.remediation: Replace that Consequences sentence with what the receipt records: the gate window model is checked in local-dev with quint 0.32.0 and openjdk 21, both invariants NoError under quint verify at 44 steps, the tightness witness refuted and mutants m8 and m9 killed; keep DESIGNED_NOT_BUILT only for the axis architecture.md:2050 still records as Blocked, and name the receipt path so a reader can rerun it. Non-blocking: it understates the evidence the delta carries and no behaviour depends on it.

findings.obligation: For each failure point or bypass the design names, a test observes the degraded outcome or the closing statement says why it is unreachable, and a degradation bound is a stated measurable value a check can trip (nw-code-craftsmanship 30, 32); a refusal or guard states WHAT, WHY and HOW with the facts the rejecting code holds (gate:self-explaining-what-why-how).
findings.observation: ADR-IIS-SKR-003 Decision states "Above the envelope the gate is not safe, which K6 states and Y11 owns, with I-28a as the backstop", and architecture.md:2358 (Y11) states "A server set above the 20 s envelope can still be read as stale ... I-28a is the backstop for both". The shipped I-28a copy at crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/handlers/secrets_key.rs:97 is "Type START OVER to confirm that no Foundry server of an earlier release is still running." - it names only the earlier-release hazard and says nothing about a reload setting, so an operator who honestly types START OVER has not ruled out the envelope hazard the design assigns to this same sentence. Nothing bounds the setting either: crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/config.rs:271 is `Duration::from_millis(whole_number(&get, RELOAD_MS, DEFAULT_RELOAD_MS)?.max(1))`, a floor of 1 ms and no ceiling, which K6 itself records. The consequence is concrete and is the same class of defect this delta fixed, moved to a different setting: a uniformly configured deployment at FOUNDRY_INTEGRATIONS_RELOAD_MS = 60000 leaves gaps of up to 70 s between beats against a fixed 40 s window, so a running opener reads as gone and Start over offers to discard credentials it is serving with. The superseded ADR-IIS-SKR-002 window (two beat intervals plus the reader's own setting, 80 s there) covered that uniform case, so the constant window introduces this region. No check trips the bound and no test observes the degraded outcome.
findings.remediation: Pick one of: refuse or warn loudly at boot when FOUNDRY_INTEGRATIONS_RELOAD_MS exceeds LiveOpeners::RELOAD_ENVELOPE, naming the value read, the 20 s envelope and that Start over is withheld or unsafe above it, with a test observing that degraded outcome; or make the gate read max(RELOAD_ENVELOPE, this server setting) so a uniformly configured deployment above the envelope stays covered and record that mixed settings above it remain out of scope; or, if the bound stays human-owned, extend the I-28a confirmation copy so the sentence the admin types actually covers the hazard Y11 assigns to it, which makes it an oracle and product change too. Non-blocking: ADR-IIS-SKR-003 is Accepted and K6/Y11 record the bound with provenance, so this is an open obligation on the accepted design, not a refusal of the implementation.

Implementation against its immutable oracle and consumed design, read on the delta 55d042b..HEAD. LiveOpeners now holds the clock instant alone; `at(now)` takes no reload argument, so a call site cannot widen or narrow the window - the wrong state is unrepresentable rather than runtime-checked. WINDOW is `2 * BEAT_EVERY + RELOAD_ENVELOPE` = 40 s, with BEAT_EVERY read from crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/reload.rs:30 and REPLICA_STATE_RETENTION from crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/worker.rs:74; both changed by visibility only, private to pub(crate), so neither constant is restated beside the gate and no owner moved. That is exactly ADR-IIS-SKR-003's Decision. `gate_of` lost its Integrations parameter at every one of its five call sites (handlers/instance.rs:581, 1001, 1081, 1388; handlers/secrets_key.rs:327, 450, 472, 529), and handlers/secrets_key.rs:472 still re-reads the same gate inside the POST, which the store applies under its own locked transaction, so the apply half of L12 is the same constant window as the page half. I verified the test's `longest_beat_gap` model against the real rule at reload.rs:157 (`due = last_beat.is_none_or(|at| now - at >= BEAT_EVERY)` on a reload tick): the gap is BEAT_EVERY rounded up to whole reload intervals, and the model matches, with +BEAT_EVERY of lateness margin. At the envelope edge the bound is tight and holds: a 20 s writer leaves at most 30 s, plus one beat interval is exactly the 40 s window. No anemic entity, no application transaction script holding a domain decision, no runtime check that a type could exclude, and no new generic payload at a boundary.

Oracle completeness and discrimination for the delta's two new laws, judged against the original Request's "while the stored secrets key cannot be opened, Replace is withheld and the page offers Start over ... credentials it cannot open are discarded". Each declared behaviour has an executable stimulus and assertions. L12 page half: crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/instance-integration-setup.feature:1250 drives a running second server that has just beaten, then advances only the reading Foundry's clock by QUIET_BETWEEN_WORDS (20 s), which a const assert in crates/foundry-acceptance/src/support/instance_integration_setup.rs pins as strictly between BEAT_INTERVAL (10 s) and LIVE_WINDOW (40 s); it asserts the shipped I-26 words, the live-server sentence, no Start over, no Replace, and that the start-over GET leaves the stored key, the Activity and the config version untouched (then_nothing_replaced at support:2795 asserts all three, including stored_config_version). L12 apply half: feature:1529 confirms with the typed START OVER in that same quiet and asserts the confirm page again, no "Secrets key generated.", the same three unchanged facts, and - the real safety property - that after restarting with the original instance key the saved Slack connection still opens, so the credential was not discarded. L12 generated half and L13: the four tests in crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/secrets_key_rotation.rs assert `still_opening == (opens && age <= LAW_WINDOW)` where LAW_WINDOW is an independent 40 s literal written in the test and never read from LiveOpeners::WINDOW, over writer 1..=20000 ms, reader 1..=3_600_000 ms and u64::MAX ms, ages -10 s..=120 s and both truth values of the row, plus the named triples including the 5000 ms writer read at 24 s by a 200 ms reader that the refused window answers wrongly, and LAW_WINDOW < REPLICA_STATE_RETENTION read where each constant is owned. Discrimination is observed, not argued: at f36b357 these same two scenarios failed and the rest passed. The writer and reader axes of the property cannot reach the gate by construction and carry no discriminating power of their own; the discriminating content is the age sweep against the independent literal and the beat-gap coverage, which is sufficient. The acceptance support restates BEAT_INTERVAL, RELOAD_ENVELOPE and LIVE_WINDOW as its own constants rather than importing the production ones, which are pub(crate) and unreachable from that crate; that independence is what keeps the check non-circular, so it is not a duplication defect. No test was weakened, narrowed, softened or skipped in this delta: the feature file gains two scenarios and no shipped scenario or assertion changed, the support's BEAT_WAIT is re-expressed as BEAT_INTERVAL * 3 / 2 and stays 15 s, and the step file only adds one given/when pair. scripts/examine-foundry changes are probe states and a per-replica env seam, not a test path.

diagnostic:
Accepted. The delta 55d042b..HEAD corrects the D5 safety defect at the only place that can own the window and the oracle observes the correction through the public page, with two non-blocking findings open against the accepted design.

Implementation: LiveOpeners::at(now) takes the clock alone, so no call site can reach the window at all - the defect class is now unrepresentable rather than runtime-checked - and WINDOW = 2 * BEAT_EVERY + RELOAD_ENVELOPE = 40 s reads BEAT_EVERY and REPLICA_STATE_RETENTION where reload.rs and worker.rs own them, each widened to pub(crate) only. That is ADR-IIS-SKR-003's Decision, unaltered. All five gate_of call sites follow, and the POST re-reads the same gate inside the store's locked transaction, so the apply half of L12 is the same constant as the page half. I checked the test's beat-gap model against the real rule at reload.rs:157 and it matches; the bound is tight and holds at the envelope edge (a 20 s writer leaves at most 30 s, plus one beat interval is exactly 40 s). No paradigm finding: no anemic entity, no domain decision in an application script, no runtime check a type could exclude.

Oracle: every declared behaviour of the delta has an executable stimulus and real assertions. The page half is observed at feature:1250 and the apply half at feature:1529, the latter asserting the credential still opens after the instance key is restored, which is the irreversible loss the law exists to prevent; the generated half and L13 are the four secrets_key_rotation.rs tests, which assert against an independent 40 s literal and never read LiveOpeners::WINDOW. Discrimination is observed rather than argued: the host's RED at f36b357 failed exactly these two scenarios (30 passed, 2 failed) and nothing else. No test was weakened, narrowed or skipped; the acceptance support's own restatement of the window is what keeps the check non-circular, not duplication, since the production constants are pub(crate) and unreachable from that crate.

Evidence: I reused the host's complete native `cargo xtask smoke` at exit 0 on a byte-identical tree for fmt, clippy, check-arch and the whole workspace test run, including all four gate-type checks, and executed the one check it excludes. The us-iis-07 lane timed out in release compilation on my first attempt (exit 124, no scenario run) and on the second attempt returned exit 0 with 32 scenarios (32 passed) and 571 steps (571 passed), both new scenarios ticked through. Nothing required is unrun.

Limits retained: Jev is unavailable (exit 3, TYPESAFE_API_KEY absent from this environment even from a shell command), so every judgment here is reviewer_reason formed locally; the project ships no test-impact selector, so selection was mechanical from the touched paths and the slice verification lists; I did not measure test timings, since no budget statement or derogation is in scope.

Open: the two design findings. The ADR Consequences paragraph still calls the Quint axis Blocked while this same delta carries the receipt that checks it, and the 20 s reload envelope the window is now sized from is bounded by nothing a check can trip, while the I-28a sentence the design names as its backstop asks only about earlier-release servers. The second is reachable - a uniform 60 s reload leaves 70 s gaps against a 40 s window - and the superseded ADR-IIS-SKR-002 window covered that case, so the constant window introduces the region. Both stay non-blocking because ADR-IIS-SKR-003 is Accepted and K6 and Y11 record the bound with provenance; they are open obligations on the accepted design, not a refusal of this implementation.
